title: asn1: Use errno and expert items instead of DISSECTOR_ASSERT for get real
description:
Handle the ASN.1 real type much closer to correctly. Report EINVAL for
illegal encodings or ERANGE for overflow and underflow, with the
appropriate rounded result. Also round if the precision is too great,
though it doesn't do the exactly proper thing if the mantissa starts
with an whole octet or more of leading zero bits (which is silly, but
allowed in BER.)

Add expert infos in the BER and PER dissectors as appropriate.

Use the log base 2 of the base so that we can call ldexp once instead
of pow twice, since ldexp is made for precisely this sort of thing.
We almost surely are on a machine where FLT_RADIX is 2 so this is
natural. If you're compiling on a S/390 or z/Architecture in a way
that has FLT_RADIX 16, good news, though - overflow will be reported
correctly for your platform.

Fix #17659. Ping #17934.

AI-Assisted: no

notes.body:
> If you're compiling on a S/390 or z/Architecture in a way that has FLT_RADIX 16, good news, though - overflow will be reported correctly for your platform.

[I would bet a silk pajama](https://compendium.vuduc.org/poem94.html) that it'd be FLT_RADIX 2, by default, on the only S/390 and ~~S/3100~~*z/Architecture* OS we support, Linux. (It probably would have been 2 by default on [Solaris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenSolaris_for_System_z) had the port shipped.) I suspect that, on Linux, any IBM compiler that's supported defaults to IEEE floating point; I don't know whether either GCC or Clang support hexadecimal floating point. For other OSes EBCDIC might raise its head as an issue for anyone ambitious enough to try a port.
(Our DCE RPC dissection code punts on VAX, Cray, and IBM hexadecimal floating point support.)

> I don't know whether either GCC or Clang support hexadecimal floating point.

I do now, at least for GCC 15.2 and Clang 22.1.0 - the answer appears to be "no", unless I'm missing an option [for GCC](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-15.2.0/gcc/S_002f390-and-zSeries-Options.html) and [for Clang](https://releases.llvm.org/22.1.0/tools/clang/docs/ClangCommandLineReference.html). (I'm guessing `-msoft-float` is for use on pre-CMOS-microprocessor systems lacking IEEE floating-point support. The LLVM folk call z/Architecture "SystemZ" there.)
Should we change the signature of `asn1_get_real()` and have it return the errno value through a pointer?

The C specification leaves it implementation defined whether `math_errhandling` is a macro that evaluates to a constant (that can be used by a preprocessor conditional) or a macro that evaluates to a symbol with external linkage (so that it can't.) On macOS it's the latter, but clang with warn about unreachable code on platforms where it's the former. Glibc also warns that it just defines `math_errhandling` to be the bitwise OR of `MATH_ERRNO` and `MATH_ERREXCEPT` but individual functions might implement one or the other, or both (`ldexp` does both.) macOS (Darwin) also never sets errno for math functions. Anyway, easier just to test both, which is supposed to work everywhere.

It could be done, though it is repeating the word. POSIX strtod does indicate EINVAL, but not Glib.

It occurs to me that since X.690 says "If the real value is the value plus zero, there shall be no contents octets in the encoding," (8.5.2) that does imply that if the return value of g_ascii_strtod is zero, it must be either a failed encoding, or something where a floating point number equal to zero was encoded not according to the 8.5.2 and the spec but via 8.5.8, so EINVAL is appropriate.
